  type: table

<!--
  Written by Claude (an AI model made by Anthropic) at Tyler George's direction.

  The explore-mode page. The game is drawn on the <canvas> below by the
  JavaScript files in the explore/ folder, starting with explore/main.js.

  When JavaScript is working, the game fills the whole browser window
  (see explore/layout.js). Without JavaScript this is an ordinary page
  with a list of links.

  Everything that matters for getting around (the way back to the
  traditional site, and the list of places under the map) is ordinary
  HTML, so it works for screen readers and when JavaScript is off.
-->

::: {#game-area .game-area}
```{=html}
<!-- The bar across the top of the game. The link back to the
     traditional site lives here so that it is ALWAYS on screen. -->
<div class="game-bar">
  <span id="scene-label" aria-live="polite">Outside</span>
  <span class="game-bar-buttons">
    <!-- Hidden until the game fills the window (see layout.js); before
         that, the list of places is simply further down the page. -->
    <button id="all-places-button" class="btn" type="button" hidden>All places</button>
    <!-- Two wordings: the long one on wide screens, the short one on
         phones, where the bar has less room (see explore.css). -->
    <a class="btn to-traditional" href="about.html"><span class="wide-only">Switch to traditional site</span><span class="narrow-only">Traditional site</span></a>
  </span>
</div>

<!-- The strip between the bar and the map. Whatever the player walks
     up to is described HERE, always in the same place, so nothing ever
     covers the map. panel.js fills it in. aria-live makes screen
     readers read it out when it changes. -->
<div class="game-talk">
  <p id="talk-idle">Walk up to something to find out about it.</p>
  <div id="place-panel" aria-live="polite" hidden>
    <img id="place-image" alt="Preview of the website this leads to" hidden>
    <div class="place-text">
      <strong id="place-title"></strong>
      <span id="place-description"></span>
    </div>
    <div class="place-buttons">
      <button id="place-enter" class="btn" type="button" hidden>Go inside (Enter)</button>
      <a id="place-link" class="btn" href="#">Open page</a>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- The "stage": the map, with the start hint and name tags laid over it. -->
<div class="game-stage">

<!-- Shown only if JavaScript is off or broken; main.js hides it. -->
<p id="game-fallback">
  The walkable map needs JavaScript. Every place on it is listed below.
</p>

<!-- The game. It starts hidden; main.js reveals it once it is running.
     width/height must match VIEW_COLS x TILE and VIEW_ROWS x TILE in
     explore/config.js. tabindex="0" lets keyboard users Tab to it. -->
<canvas id="game-canvas" width="320" height="224" tabindex="0" hidden
  aria-label="Walkable pixel-art campus. Use the arrow keys or W, A, S, D to walk. Everything here is also available on the traditional site.">
</canvas>

<!-- Sits on top of the map until the visitor starts the game. -->
<button id="game-start-hint" type="button" hidden>
  Click here to start walking<br>
  <small>Move with the arrow keys or W A S D</small>
</button>

<!-- Name tags that float above things in a room. labels.js fills
     this in. aria-hidden: screen readers get the same names from the
     pop-up instead, so they are not read twice. -->
<div id="thing-labels" aria-hidden="true"></div>

<!-- The conversation box (talking to the fairy). dialogue.js fills it
     in. aria-live makes screen readers read each line as it appears. -->
<div id="dialogue" aria-live="polite" hidden>
  <strong id="dialogue-speaker"></strong>
  <p id="dialogue-text"></p>
  <button id="dialogue-next" class="btn" type="button">Next</button>
</div>

<!-- A white cover that fades in over the map when the player steps
     through a portal (see warp.js). It never takes clicks. -->
<div id="warp-flash"></div>

</div><!-- end of game-stage -->

<!-- The large pop-up for reading part of the regular site without
     leaving the game. reader.js fills it in. <dialog> is the browser's
     built-in pop-up: Esc closes it and the page behind is dimmed. -->
<dialog id="reader" aria-labelledby="reader-title">
  <div class="reader-bar">
    <strong id="reader-title"></strong>
    <button id="reader-close" class="btn" type="button">Close (Esc)</button>
  </div>
  <div id="reader-content"></div>
  <p class="reader-foot">
    <a id="reader-source" href="#" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open this on the regular site (new tab)</a>
  </p>
</dialog>

<script type="module" src="explore/main.js"></script>
```
:::
